question: What relative contents of N-5 and N-6 did the lignite char have after fast pyrolysis at 800 °C?
trap: the raw lignite's 51% / 26% or the sawdust char's 42% / 40%
rendered:
<document title="Effects of sodium on nitrogen evolution characteristics during the fast co-pyrolysis of coal and biomass">

=== page 5 ===
- For the LC sample pyrolyzed at 500 °C, the relative content of N-5 decreased, whereas N-6 and N-Q increased slightly (Fig. 4e).
- During fast pyrolysis at 800 °C, the N-A in SD completely decomposed (Fig. 4c).
- The resulting char-N distribution was dominated by N-5 (42%) and N-6 (40%).
- At high temperatures, a portion of N-5 is released as volatiles (specically HCN) via ring-opening reactions, while the remainder converts into N-Q and the more thermally stable N-6.^24,31 As for the LC char pyrolyzed at 800 °C, as shown in Fig. 4f, char-N consisted of N-5, N-6, and N-Q, while N-X was completely volatilized.^35

Answer: N-5 (42%), N-6 (40%).
